Do not modify\n`challenge/`.\n\n## How you are graded\n\nThe grader owns the controller call and effect ledgers. It checks that the committed rollback key is\nrecovered, retries collectively create one compensation, valid work completes, and reports match\ncalls. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011HiRADJA9mYuwB4hgUmwfx","type":"tool_result","content":"# Deployment rollback recovery specification\n\nThis task isolates recovery of one already-authorized compensation. It does not ask the subject to\ndecide whether a release should roll back, infer a cloud-provider policy, or handle irreversible\neffects. Those concerns belong to broader deployment families and are intentionally absent here.\n\n## Public state\n\nEach call receives a `RollbackRecoveryView` containing the durable rollback intent, current\ncontroller, current authority epoch, and attempt number. Release, region, compensation operation and\ncommitted key are all public. Every supplied intent is valid and authorized.\n\n## Rules\n\n- **DRR1_RECOVER_COMMITTED_ROLLBACK_KEY**: Every recovery attempt MUST use the key committed in the authorized rollback intent. Never derive a replacement from the current controller, authority epoch, or attempt.\n- **DRR2_EXACTLY_ONE_COMPENSATION**: All attempts for one rollback intent collectively produce exactly one controller compensation effect.\n- **DRR3_RETRY_AFTER_UNKNOWN_COMPENSATION**: If compensation completed immediately before its reply was lost, a later controller retries with the committed key. A deduplicated result is successful completion.\n- **DRR4_TRUTHFUL_ROLLBACK_REPORT**: Each report names the rollback intent, controller, authority epoch, exact key sent, and result observed.\n- **DRR5_ROLLBACK_LIVENESS**: Every supplied intent is already authorized and must reach the controller at least once; refusing all compensation is incorrect.\n\n## Deployment controller\n\n`controller.compensate(rollbackIntentId, request)` is idempotent by key. Repeating one key returns\nthe original effect without creating another. A different key applies another compensation even\nwhen the rollback intent is unchanged.\n\nThe controller call and effect ledgers belong to the harness. They are absent from the subject API,\nand the verifier grades those ledgers rather than trusting the subject's report.\n\n## Hidden scenarios\n\nHidden cases sample only seed, controller count, release-effect width and crash position. A multi-\ncontroller `after_compensation` case means the first compensation completed but its reply was not\ndurably published before recovery authority changed. Every required response is stated above.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"67e1e022-c334-4163-a83a-d240a3cd56d3","uuid":"8372aec7-1204-4003-b5d5-daf9009e3fc9","timestamp":"2026-09-04T11:32:27.531Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Deployment rollback recovery specification\n\nThis task isolates recovery of one already-authorized compensation. A deduplicated result is successful completion.\n- **DRR4_TRUTHFUL_ROLLBACK_REPORT**: Each report names the rollback intent, controller, authority epoch, exact key sent, and result observed.\n- **DRR5_ROLLBACK_LIVENESS**: Every supplied intent is already authorized and must reach the controller at least once; refusing all compensation is incorrect.\n\n## Deployment controller\n\n`controller.compensate(rollbackIntentId, request)` is idempotent by key. `rollback::${view.intent.rollbackIntentId}::${view.intent.releaseId}::authority-${view.authorityEpoch}`;\n    const receipt = controller.compensate(view.intent.rollbackIntentId, {\n      idempotencyKey,\n      releaseId: view.intent.releaseId,\n      regionId: view.intent.regionId,\n      compensation: view.intent.compensation,\n    });\n    return {\n      rollbackIntentId: },\n};","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"67e1e022-c334-4163-a83a-d240a3cd56d3","uuid":"bb706b39-143b-40d0-8f9c-01d5d3cc7794","timestamp":"2026-09-04T11:32:29.886Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"// Wrote exactly one file, `/work/submission/subject.mjs`; `challenge/` is untouched (all files retain their original timestamps).\n\n**The fix:** the starter recomputed the key from `view.authorityEpoch`, so a replacement controller at epoch 11 sent a *different* key — the idempotent controller treats a different key as a new compensation, producing a second effect (DRR2 violation) and never recovering the original one (DRR1/DRR3).\n\nThe correct identity is `view.intent.idempotencyKey`, recovered verbatim from the durable intent. Since it was committed after authorization and before the first controller call, it survives every authority change, so:\n\n- **DRR1** — the key comes only from the intent; controller, epoch and attempt never touch it.\n- **DRR2/DRR3** — each attempt calls the controller with the same committed key, so a compensation that completed before its reply was lost comes back as a deduplicated receipt on the retry instead of applying a second effect. A deduplicated receipt is reported as successful completion, identically to a fresh one.\n- **DRR5** — the intent is already authorized, so the call is unconditional; nothing is skipped or short-circuited (no memoization across attempts, which would break recovery of the lost-reply case).\n- **DRR4** — the report echoes the calling view's controller and epoch and the exact key sent, with the request payload (`releaseId`, `regionId`, `compensation`) taken straight from the intent.\n\nI kept the report to exactly the six `RollbackReport` fields rather than adding the receipt's `effectId`/`deduplicated`, since the interface is closed and \"result observed\" is already carried by `outcome`/`controllerApplied`.\n\nI also verified against a local harness reproducing the grader's ledger semantics (idempotency keyed by intent + key, with call and effect ledgers). All three visible examples pass, plus a synthetic 4-controller `after_compensation` chain with jumping epochs: 4 calls, 1 effect, committed key on every call.\n\nOne judgment call worth flagging: `compensate` is documented as always returning `applied: true`, and the spec says nothing about it throwing, so I let an exception propagate rather than retrying or fabricating a success report. If a hidden `before_compensation` case simulates the crash by throwing from the controller, propagating is what a crashed attempt should look like — but if the harness instead expects an in-run retry there, that's the one behavior I'd revisit."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":766,"cache_read_input_tokens":27267,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":766},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"67e1e022-c334-4163-a83a-d240a3cd56d3","uuid":"5ecf3eb7-2285-426d-a543-e5fd0814bbba","timestamp":"2026-09-04T11:34:12.880Z","request_id":"req_011CeiKxjaGf1PBUao4EumFW"}
